findings_qualitative.value: The broad CO component at 26.5 km s^-1 previously linked to AG Car by Nota et al. (2002) is resolved out by ACA and corresponds to extended ambient gas, whereas a newly identified component at 32.5 km s^-1 (29 to 36 km s^-1) forms a compact circumstellar ring.

findings_qualitative.value: The molecular ring is aligned with the SE-NW elongation of the infrared shell and perpendicular in projection to the optical continuum jet, placing it near the stellar equatorial plane.

evidence.quote: Considering this, we can safely assume that the ring lies in –or at least close to– the equatorial plane of the star.

findings_qualitative.value: An equatorially enhanced mass outflow (possibly driven by rotationally-induced bistability in a pre-LBV or LBV phase) is the most promising formation scenario for the molecular ring, which subsequently shaped the younger bipolar nebula via wind-wind interaction.

claims.hypothesis: A circumstellar molecular ring or disk surrounds the LBV star AG Car, as originally suggested from single-dish SEST spectra by Nota et al. (2002).
claims.experiment: Mapped CO J=3-2 with APEX and CO J=2-1 and 13CO J=2-1 with ALMA ACA and Total Power arrays.
claims.result: ACA filters out the 26.5 km s^-1 component proposed by N02 (showing it is extended ambient gas), but resolves a 35x15 arcsec elliptical ring around AG Car at v_LSR = 29 to 36 km s^-1 (centred at 32.5 km s^-1) expanding at 3.5 +/- 0.5 km s^-1.
claims.finding: A slowly expanding molecular ring encloses AG Car near its equatorial plane, though it corresponds to a different velocity component (32.5 km s^-1) than the one tentatively identified by N02.

evidence.quote: The interferometer filtered out most of the emission at $v_\mathrm{LSR} <$ 30 km s$^{-1}$, including the broad line at 26.5 km s$^{-1}$.
Such improvement allows us to resolve the emission, revealing an elliptical structure enclosing AG Car and apparently detached from the star.
Correcting for the inclination, we estimate an expansion velocity of $v_\mathrm{exp}=3.5\pm0.5$ km s$^{-1}$.

claims.hypothesis: The molecular ring gas is physically distinct from the cold foreground/background ISM clouds and accounts for a substantial fraction of the total mass ejected by AG Car.
claims.experiment: Performed non-LTE RADEX modelling of single-dish CO J=2-1, 13CO J=2-1, and CO J=3-2 line intensities and derived the molecular gas mass.
claims.result: The ring gas is warm (T_k = 50 K), moderately dense (n(H2) = 1.3x10^3 cm^-3), and moderately optically thick (tau_21 = 1.2, tau_32 = 0.8), with R_12/13 = 25 +/- 4 and a total molecular mass of 2.7 +/- 0.9 M_sun.
claims.finding: The ring exhibits excitation conditions distinct from the optically thin ambient ISM components and accounts for at least ~30% of the total mass lost by AG Car.

evidence.quote: We find that the model that best fits the observations is that with $T_\mathrm{k}$ = 50 K, $N(\mathrm{CO})$ = 2.4$\times10^{16}$ cm$^{-2}$ and $n\mathrm{(H_2)}$ = 1.3$\times10^3$ cm$^{-3}$.
The total mass of molecular gas in the ring is $2.7\pm0.9$ M$_{\ensuremath{\odot}}$.

evidence.loc: Mass loss history of AG Car
evidence.quote: This means that, assuming a stellar origin, the molecular gas around AG Car traces at least a $\sim30\%$ of the mass lost by the star.

claims.hypothesis: The velocity structure of the molecular ring can be explained by a simple radially expanding axisymmetric torus.
claims.experiment: Constructed four 3D non-LTE radiative transfer models in LIME (pure rotation, pure expansion, expansion + differential rotation, and expansion + macro-turbulence) and compared synthetic channel maps with ACA observations.
claims.result: Pure rotation fails to match the velocity extent, while pure radial expansion reproduces the lobes and clockwise pattern but fails to reproduce the connecting arcs at intermediate velocities (29.5-30.8 and 34.6-35.9 km s^-1), which are only reproduced when adding rotation or macro-turbulence.
claims.finding: Deviations from pure radial expansion—either macro-turbulence or a differential rotational component—are required to reproduce all observed morpho-kinematic features of the ring.

evidence.loc: A closer view to CO kinematics
evidence.quote: Still, we note that the arc-like features that connect the lobes at intermediate velocities (from 29.5 to 30.77 and 34.58 to 35.85 km s$^{-1}$) can only be reproduced by models 3 and 4, i.e. if we add rotation or turbulence to the expanding ring.

We develop a simple kinematic model to better study gas dynamics, showing that some deviations from pure radial expansion are required to properly reproduce some of the morpho-kinematic features observed in the data, such as: (1) the addition of a turbulent component or (2) the superposition of a differential rotational field.

claims.hypothesis: The millimetre continuum emission from the central point source traces the current ionized stellar wind of AG Car.
claims.experiment: Fitted a 2D Gaussian to the central compact source at 225 GHz, compared with historical ATCA 5.5 and 8.8 GHz fluxes, and applied the Panagia & Felli (1975) free-free wind mass-loss formula.
claims.result: Measured a point-source flux density of 30.2 +/- 2.2 mJy, yielding a current mass-loss rate of (1.55 +/- 0.21) x 10^-5 M_sun yr^-1, which matches the quiescent mass-loss rate of 1.5 x 10^-5 M_sun yr^-1 from Groh et al. (2009).
claims.finding: The 225 GHz central point source is consistent with thermal emission from the current stellar wind, confirming a quiescent mass-loss rate of ~1.55 x 10^-5 M_sun yr^-1.

why_this_data.value: Previous SEST single-dish CO observations had coarse angular resolution (45 and 23 arcsec), so higher-resolution ALMA/ACA interferometric mapping combined with Total Power and APEX single-dish data was needed to resolve the circumstellar structure while recovering all spatial scales.

evidence.quote: Despite this promising result, the region was never properly imaged at higher resolution to confirm the existence of such a structure.

Finally, to recover all the spatial scales and avoid missing flux, we combined the ACA and the Total Power (hereafter ALMA TP) cubes with the CASA `feather` task, which involved regridding the single-dish data and correcting it for the primary beam response.

why_this_method.value: RADEX non-LTE modelling of single-dish data was used because interferometric CO J=3-2 data were unavailable; qualitative LIME 3D modelling was chosen over formal fitting to avoid overinterpreting maps with modest spatial (~7 arcsec) and spectral (1.3 km s^-1) resolution.

evidence.quote: However, the analysis is restricted to the single-dish data, i.e. APEX and ALMA TP, since we lack interferometric CO $J=3\rightarrow2$ observations.

evidence.loc: A closer view to CO kinematics

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Isolating the 32.5 km s^-1 component in the APEX cube by subtracting neighbouring Gaussian components was attempted but rejected because it introduced artefacts that altered the line shape.

evidence.quote: We attempted to isolate the line by removing the neighbouring components through a gaussian fitting, but this resulted in the introduction of multiple artefacts that altered the line shape.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Accretion disk of infalling gas rejected as the kinematic explanation for the radial velocity gradient because infalling disks are only expected in pre-main-sequence stages, whereas AG Car is an evolved star.

evidence.quote: Two physical scenarios are possible: (1) an accretion disc of gas falling onto the star; or (2), an expanding ring, composed of stellar ejecta or compressed interstellar gas.
From an evolutionary perspective, the accretion disk scenario is highly improbable.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: RADEX solutions with kinetic temperatures T_k > 120 K rejected because they require diffuse-cloud volume densities (~100 cm^-3) well below the CO J=2-1 critical density.

evidence.quote: Regarding the temperature, though, solutions for $T_\mathrm{k}>120$ K are unlikely: the required volume densities are comparable to those of diffuse clouds ($\sim$ 100 cm$^{-3}$), falling well below the critical density of the $J=2\rightarrow1$ transition.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Purely rotating ring (LIME model 1) rejected because it concentrates emission around the systemic velocity and fails to reproduce the shape and velocity extent of the ring.

evidence.loc: A closer view to CO kinematics
evidence.quote: Not surprisingly, the rotating ring (model 1) fails to reproduce the shape and velocity extent of the ring, with all the emission significantly concentrated around the systemic velocity.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Swept-up pre-existing natal cloud material and binary interaction/merger scenarios considered less likely than an equatorially enhanced mass outflow, since AG Car sits inside a 9 pc evacuated cavity and lacks detected binary companions.

evidence.quote: Should the CO arise from compressed ISM material, one would expect to find it farther from the star, toward the edges of a wind-blown bubble.
We regard the mass outflow as the most promising, taking into account the evolutionary stage of the star and the evidence available.

limitations_admitted.value: Large angular distance (~4 deg) to the ALMA TP off position caused spectral ripples that were not removed in post-processing.

evidence.quote: Such a large angular distance between the target and the off position caused ripples in the spectra, which we did not attempt to remove in post-processing, since their amplitude is negligible with respect to the brightness of the spectral lines from our target.

limitations_admitted.value: Fainter arcs of the ring are not detected in 13CO J=2-1 due to limited sensitivity.

evidence.quote: In the $^{13}$CO $J=2\rightarrow1$ integrated intensity map (not shown), only the lobes of the structure are visible, with an S/N ratio slightly above 5 $\sigma$.
The non-detection of fainter arcs is likely due to the limited sensitivity.

limitations_admitted.value: ACA is likely missing a fraction of the extended 225 GHz radio continuum flux because its largest angular scale is ~1/3 that of the ATCA 750B configuration at 5.5 GHz.

evidence.quote: We note, though, that the LAS (largest angular scale) of ACA at 225 GHz is about 1/3 of the LAS of ATCA 750B configuration at 5.5 GHz, so it is very likely that we are missing a fraction of the extended flux.

limitations_admitted.value: Moderate velocity resolution (1.3 km s^-1, sampling the ring across only seven channels) and contamination in the 28.2 and 29.5 km s^-1 channels limit detailed kinematic analysis and cause significant line blending.

evidence.quote: We note that the moderate velocity resolution of our data, of just 1.3 km s$^{-1}$, does not allow us to perform a detailed analysis of the observed kinematic structure, which is sampled by only seven channels.
In some cases, the fitting was rather problematic due to significant line blending, derived from the limited velocity resolution.

limitations_admitted.value: Excitation analysis is restricted to single-dish data (providing only average values affected by beam dilution) due to the lack of interferometric CO J=3-2 observations, and RADEX assumes a homogeneous medium and ignores source geometry.

evidence.quote: However, the analysis is restricted to the single-dish data, i.e. APEX and ALMA TP, since we lack interferometric CO $J=3\rightarrow2$ observations.
And second, it works under the assumption of a homogeneous medium, meaning that all transitions sample the same gas volume with the same excitation conditions.

limitations_admitted.value: The molecular ring mass estimate is strongly affected by uncertainties in the X_CO abundance factor, which could be lower in C- and O-deficient LBV nebulae.

evidence.quote: It is worth to highlight that this estimate is strongly affected by the determination of the $X_\mathrm{CO}$ factor and its associated uncertainties.

limitations_admitted.value: The kinematic duration and average mass-loss rate of the ring are loose limits because the ring width is unresolved (conservatively set to the 7 arcsec ACA beam) and constant expansion velocity with zero dispersion is assumed.

evidence.loc: Mass loss history of AG Car
evidence.quote: However, we warn that the reliability of this method is limited, in the sense that the emitting region may be smaller than the beam; therefore, we decided to conservatively adopt the size of the ACA beam, of about 7$''$, as the reference ’width’ of the ring.

evidence.loc: Mass loss history of AG Car
evidence.quote: In addition, we work under the assumption that the expansion velocity does not change and there is no velocity dispersion across the ring, which is probably unrealistic.

referee_caveats_inferred: The excitation modelling relies on conservative upper limits for the single-dish beam-filling factors (F <= 0.2 and F <= 0.38) rather than directly using the ACA-resolved ring solid angle, which directly impacts the derived column density and optical depth.
Only two transitions of 12CO (2-1 and 3-2) are used in the chi^2 minimization to constrain three RADEX parameters (T_k, N(CO), n(H2)), leaving temperature and density largely degenerate.

Severe blending between the ring component C4 (32.5-33.7 km s^-1) and the narrow ambient component C3 (29.6 km s^-1) introduces systematic uncertainty in the Gaussian decomposition and integrated flux of the ring.

Adopting the canonical 6 kpc distance rather than the Gaia-revised 4.7 kpc distance affects the derived physical radius, molecular gas mass (~39% lower at 4.7 kpc), and mass-loss rate (~30% lower at 4.7 kpc).
